summary.added_external_crate_count_note: P2-G4 adds no package to Cargo.lock. The sandbox backends need libc on Unix and windows-sys on Windows; both are already resolved in this lock through earlier reviewed receipts (libc through libsqlite3-sys, windows-sys through academic-keystore-platform and academic-store-platform), at the same pinned versions. What is new is two direct edges, recorded below, and one workspace path package.
summary.added_workspace_path_package_note: academic-worker is a seventh package and deliberately not a seventh process class. The six P2-G7 process packages are pinned whole by six_process_entrypoints_are_exact_and_distinct and this task does not touch them: the worker holds no ProcessClass, no capability from that matrix, and no outbound socket capability. Nothing in the workspace depends on academic-worker, which is what keeps its probe binary out of every other crate's graph.

libc.edge: crates/worker, [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies], optional, behind the non-default native-sandbox feature
libc.features: default-features = false, features = ["std"]. No extra_traits, no align, no rustc-dep-of-std.
libc.why_this_dependency_belongs_inside_its_t: The Linux backend is four syscalls — setrlimit, prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS), the three landlock_* calls, and seccomp(SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER). libc is the declaration of those numbers and of the rlimit and rusage structures, nothing more; the seccomp BPF program and the two Landlock structures are defined in this crate because libc does not carry them. Writing the declarations by hand instead was considered and rejected: extern "C" blocks, #[link] and no_mangle are refused anywhere in a workspace crate by only_egress_crate_has_a_socket's third half, so a hand-rolled binding would have had to weaken that rule.
libc.advisory_path: Unchanged. libc is already triaged through the Phase 1 receipt's advisory path; this adds an edge to an existing pinned version, not a version.

windows-sys.edge: crates/worker, [target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies], optional, behind the non-default native-sandbox feature
windows-sys.features: Win32_Foundation, Win32_Security, Win32_Security_Authorization, Win32_Security_Isolation, Win32_Storage_FileSystem, Win32_System_JobObjects, Win32_System_Threading. Win32_Security_Isolation and Win32_System_JobObjects are new to this workspace; the other five are already selected by academic-store-platform, academic-vault, academic-keystore-platform or academic-daemon. windows-sys resolves no package per feature, so the lock is unchanged.
windows-sys.why_this_dependency_belongs_inside_its_t: The Windows backend is an AppContainer profile, a DACL entry for its SID on three directories, a process-thread attribute list carrying SECURITY_CAPABILITIES, and a job object with ActiveProcessLimit, ProcessMemoryLimit and PerProcessUserTimeLimit. Every one of those is a Win32 call with no safe-Rust equivalent, and the same foreign-function rule that applies to libc applies here. Win32_Networking_WinSock is deliberately not selected: the parent never touches a socket, and only_egress_crate_has_a_socket would refuse the WSA* spellings it brings.
windows-sys.advisory_path: Unchanged. windows-sys is already triaged through the Phase 1 receipt's advisory path; this adds an edge and two feature flags to an existing pinned version.

why_this_dependency_belongs_inside_its_t: academic-worker is a workspace path crate, not an external dependency. It owns the P2-G4 containment boundary: the per-job capability descriptor, the staged input/output pair, the core-only acceptance of a staged output, the resource receipt every model run is paired with, and the two measured operating-system backends. It is the one place in this workspace that holds unsafe code outside the four reviewed platform leaves, and unsafe_is_confined_to_the_sandbox_backends in crates/worker/tests/capability.rs is what keeps that to the two backend files.
network_posture: The crate's product source opens no socket. Its Linux backend names the socket syscall numbers, and only to put them in a seccomp deny list, which only_egress_crate_has_a_socket checks structurally by requiring every SYS_ spelling in that file to appear inside its denied_syscalls function. The probe binary under crates/worker/probes does name TcpStream and TcpListener, because a test that proves the operating system refuses a socket has to ask for one; it is a [[bin]] with required-features = ["native-sandbox"] and a path outside src, no workspace crate depends on academic-worker, and both facts are read out of cargo metadata by that same scan. product_network stays NONE.
advisory_path: Unchanged. Both external crates this task reaches were admitted by earlier receipts at these exact versions and are triaged through them. .github/dependabot.yml opens no version-update pull request.
